Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

pleasure noun

also enjoyment, delight, a pleasure, delight (verb)

classical

Cic. Fam. 5.7.1: ex litterīs tuīs … cēpī ūnā cum omnibus incrēdibilem voluptātem
Cic. Fin. 1.37 (Lewis & Short): omne id, quō gaudēmus, voluptās est
Cic. Fam. 14.1.4: utinam ea rēs eī voluptātī sit!
Traupman 361

voluptās, voluptātis f.

noun, third declension

pleasure, enjoyment, delight

Pleasure of every kind, of the body or of the mind; the philosophers’ word for ἡδονή, so in moral writing often the pleasure one should not chase. “It gives me pleasure”: voluptātem capiō ex, or mihi voluptātī est. In comedy voluptās mea is “my darling” (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • dēlectātiō, dēlectātiōnis f. — delight, amusement

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Off. 1.105 (Lewis & Short): homō videndī et audiendī dēlectātiōne dūcitur

    The delight a thing gives, especially of seeing, hearing and learning; it never has the bad sense voluptās can have. The verb is dēlectāre (see enjoy).

  • dēlectō, dēlectāre, dēlectāvī, dēlectātum — delight, please

    verb, first conjugation · also used · classical · Traupman 302

Examples

  • ex litterīs tuīs, quās pūblicē mīsistī, cēpī ūnā cum omnibus incrēdibilem voluptātem

    your official letter gave me, as it gave everyone, enormous pleasureCic. Fam. 5.7.1

  • cibī pōtiōnisque dēsīderiō nātūrālī, nōn voluptāte modus fīnītus

    the measure of his food and drink was set by natural need, not by pleasureLiv. 21.4.6

  • Nē timē, voluptās mea.

    Don’t be afraid, my darling.Plaut. Mil. 1345

  • suō arbitriō

    at their own pleasureTraupman 361

  • magnam voluptātem capere ex aliquā rē

    to derive great pleasure from somethingTraupman 361

See also enjoy, with pleasure, you’re welcome, fun, glad, desire.
